assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat-band physics of twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform for correlated and superconducting states in a tunable two-dimensional material. It is a clear case of a prediction from continuum band theory meeting a striking experimental discovery, which is the theory-experiment link I value most. It also created the field of moire quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation identified the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Cao and colleagues) observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. Theory plus experiment fits a three-person prize. Other experimental groups contributed to the follow-up, so the boundary of credit is imperfect, but the core is identifiable.
assessment.maturity: Observations have been reproduced by many independent groups and with several materials in under a decade, and the theory explains the main features. Some details of the superconducting pairing remain debated, but the central discovery is firmly established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Sample-to-sample variation and twist-angle disorder complicate quantitative comparison with theory.
Other experimental contributors might claim part of the credit; I cannot verify the full priority record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, later made giant with crystalline MgO barriers, is a spin-dependent quantum transport effect whose understanding rests on electronic-structure theory of the interface. It underpins hard-disk read heads and magnetic memory, so it unites a physical discovery with large practical use.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin's group (with the Yuasa/Djayaprawira line of work) established giant TMR in MgO-based junctions. I would reserve some doubt about how credit for the MgO step is divided with colleagues not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been independently confirmed for three decades and explained by first-principles calculations of coherent tunnelling. GMR was already recognised in 2007, so this is a natural follow-on rather than a premature choice.
uncertainties: The giant MgO result involves contributors beyond the three listed names, so attribution is incomplete.
The committee may judge it too close to the 2007 GMR prize, or too technological.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators are a new state of matter with protected edge and surface states, extending band theory by a topological classification. The theory was followed by clean experiments, including transport in HgTe quantum wells and spectroscopic mapping of surface states, which is the kind of validation by spectra I find convincing.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal; Hasan's group identified 3D topological insulators by photoemission. Choosing three of the listed four is difficult, and I would leave out Mele only reluctantly. The listed set also omits several theorists who contributed essential steps.
assessment.maturity: The effect is robust, widely reproduced and spectroscopically verified. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions covers the mathematical foundation but not these discoveries, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The proper trio is contested because Mele and theorists outside the supplied credit are also decisive.
Overlap with the 2016 Haldane/Kosterlitz/Thouless prize might weigh against it for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is a non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons that made the Mott transition and correlated metals computationally tractable. Combined with DFT it is now a standard tool for real correlated materials, and it directly addresses where first-principles methods fail. I know this area well and regard its influence as very substantial.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping to an impurity problem and the DFT+DMFT extension; Vollhardt, with Metzner, introduced the infinite-dimensional limit. Metzner is not in the supplied credit, which leaves a real allocation question for the founding step.
assessment.maturity: The method has been in use for over three decades and is validated against experiments and numerically exact results. Its status as a mainstream tool is firm, though quantitative predictive success in real materials is uneven.
uncertainties: Founding credit is shared with Walter Metzner, who is not among the supplied names.
A theory-method prize needs a clear physical discovery, and some may see this as a computational tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correction of spherical aberration in electron lenses achieved sub-angstrom resolution and atomic-scale imaging and spectroscopy of materials, a defining instrument advance for condensed matter and materials physics. The Ruska prize of 1986 is a precedent for recognising electron optics.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the corrector theory, Haider and colleagues built the working hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban led its application and demonstration in materials. The three-person split follows a clear theory, construction, application line.
assessment.maturity: Correctors are commercial and routine, and independently confirmed across laboratories. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Others, notably Krivanek and co-workers on the STEM corrector, are not among the supplied names, so priority could be disputed.
Whether the committee will treat an instrumentation advance as a discovery of physics rather than technique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with controllable parameters, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and, later, single-site resolved microscopy. They give a quantum simulator of the very models I try to solve numerically, and it is a significant conceptual and experimental development.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal, the Greiner-Bloch Mott insulator observation and the Esslinger group's fermionic work are all central. The supplied list has five names, and any trio leaves out major contributors such as Cirac and Esslinger; Jaksch is absent altogether.
assessment.maturity: The experiments are widely reproduced and now reach regimes beyond classical simulation, although a decisive scientific result about a long-standing open problem such as the doped Hubbard model is still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution is hard to resolve, with five credited names and a missing proposer.
The 2012 and 2001 prizes on atomic control and condensates are adjacent, and decisive new physics from the simulators is still to come.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics gave strong light-matter coupling on a chip and the readout and control architecture for superconducting qubits. It is a basic enabling concept for quantum technology, built on the same quantum-circuit physics recognised in 2025.
assessment.attribution: Blais gave the theory, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated the strong-coupling experiment in 2004, so the trio is a coherent theory-plus-two-experiment grouping. Yale and ETH groups share credit with other circuit pioneers outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and developed in many laboratories, with widespread use. Because the 2025 prize on circuit-level quantum tunnelling is recent, the committee may prefer to wait.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize, which I chaired, raises the question of timing.
Whether the physical discovery is distinct enough from the engineering architecture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides in 2008 added a second family of non-cuprate high-Tc materials with magnetism, nematicity and multi-orbital physics entangled with superconductivity. It is a new quantum behaviour in materials that electronic-structure theory has engaged closely.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono reported superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx, and the credit is clear and compact. Later critical-temperature increases by other groups in China are outside the supplied credit and built on their discovery.
assessment.maturity: The result was confirmed within weeks by independent groups and has been explored for over fifteen years. The pairing mechanism, however, is still unsettled, which may make the committee cautious.
uncertainties: Contributions to raising Tc to about 55 K came from other groups not listed.
